question: During a microscope check of mixed liquor, an operator sees abundant filamentous organisms bridging between floc particles and a sludge volume index that keeps rising. Which finding connects those two observations to poor settling?
correctAnswer: Filaments extending from the floc slow compaction in the clarifier
explanation: Filaments that extend beyond the floc form bridges between particles, so the blanket compacts poorly and the settled volume stays high.
options: Filaments inside compact floc particles speed compaction in the clarifier
A rising sludge volume index by itself proves the clarifier rake has failed
Filaments extending from the floc slow compaction in the clarifier
Dissolved oxygen probes reading high values cause filaments to bridge floc
sourceTitle: US EPA: Municipal Wastewater — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Troubleshooting Filamentous Bulking. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Filaments inside compact floc particles speed compaction in the clarifier
optionB: A rising sludge volume index by itself proves the clarifier rake has failed
optionC: Filaments extending from the floc slow compaction in the clarifier
optionD: Dissolved oxygen probes reading high values cause filaments to bridge floc

question: Effluent ammonia rises over several cold days while aeration basin temperature falls and the solids retention time stays unchanged. Which condition most directly limits the nitrifying population in this case?
correctAnswer: Nitrifier growth slows at low temperature, so the current retention time may be too short
explanation: Nitrifiers grow slowly, and cold conditions slow them further, so a retention time that worked in warm weather may wash them out in winter.
options: Nitrifier growth speeds up at low temperature, so retention time can safely be shortened further
Nitrifier growth slows at low temperature, so the current retention time may be too short
Cold mixed liquor holds less ammonia, so the laboratory result must be a sampling container error
Low temperature removes alkalinity from the wastewater before the organisms can use it at all
sourceTitle: US EPA: Municipal Wastewater — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Troubleshooting Nitrification Loss. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Nitrifier growth speeds up at low temperature, so retention time can safely be shortened further
optionB: Nitrifier growth slows at low temperature, so the current retention time may be too short
optionC: Cold mixed liquor holds less ammonia, so the laboratory result must be a sampling container error
optionD: Low temperature removes alkalinity from the wastewater before the organisms can use it at all
